facts.text: The town’s name comes from the Choctaw word abani, meaning “to cook over a fire.”.
Between 1896 and 1920, hundreds of Hungarian immigrants settled in Albany, naming the community Árpádhon, the largest rural Hungarian settlement in the U.S. at the time.
The Hungarian Settlement School in Albany was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2001.
The old school building now houses the Hungarian Settlement Museum, which opened its doors in September 2017.
Before railroads changed everything, Albany’s economy thrived on timber, agricultural products, and manufactured goods, making it an indispensable link in Louisiana’s commercial network.
The abandoned town site now draws cultural tourists and ghost hunters, drawn by its historical significance and reported paranormal activity.
